title: Nadir Shah Carries Off Delhi’s Treasures

blocks.text: The poem now catalogs the plunder taken by Nadir Shah in language of astonishment and excess. At the center stands the Takht-e-Taus worth nine crores, alongside jewels, pearls, and courtly marvels that symbolize the prestige of the Mughal throne.

Other prized objects are listed to deepen the sense of imperial humiliation: rare gems, storied heirlooms, and even celebrated curiosities associated with musicians and kings. The conqueror strips away both treasure and aura, turning Delhi’s claims to greatness into portable spoil.

By ending on written transfers of territory and payment, the page shows that the loss was political as well as material. Lahore and its surrounding provinces appear less like secure Mughal possessions than prizes redistributed by a stronger hand.
